newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada to ease foreign bank rules - source.
newsitem.headline: Canada to ease foreign bank rules - source.

text.p: Canada will reveal plans - probably on Friday - to relax some restrictions on foreign banks operating in the country, a government source said on Thursday.
"We'll have to wait and see, probably tomorrow," the source said when asked if such an announcement was imminent.

The source said Doug Peters, secretary of state for financial institutions, would likely make the announcement in parliament on Friday afternoon, together with the introduction of separate financial services legislation.
The source confirmed newspaper reports that Ottawa planned to allow foreign banks to operate in Canada through branches, rather than through federally regulated subsidiaries.
"It's pretty close," the source said about a story in the Toronto Globe and Mail detailing of the new rules.
The story said the new foreign bank rules could take up to a year to take effect.

The higher cost of operating a subsidiary, rather than a branch, has driven several foreign banks out of the country. The number of foreign banks operating in Canada has dropped to 43 from a peak of about 60.
A federal government "white paper" on financial reforms released last summer introduced only minor changes to foreign bank rules.
After the report, both houses of the Canadian parliament issued reports urging freer access to Canada's markets for foreign banks.
Foreign bankers have complained that Canada lagged behind its Group of Seven trading partners in opening its banking sector to foreign competition.

Canada's big domestic banks have said they were willing to see foreign banks compete as branches if barriers to domestic bank mergers were removed. Federal laws discourage bank mergers by limiting investors to a maximum 10 percent stake in a Canadian bank.
The so-called Big Six dominate regular banking, trusts and brokerages in Canada, but their international rankings have slipped in recent years.
